subject.title: Talk: add context-aware durable voice sessions

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this broad durable voice-session and realtime-context configuration model in core, or should it be narrowed and staged through the existing Talk context/session seams?
rationale: The branch adds persistent state, authorization behavior, client protocol methods, outbound summaries, and substantial new configuration; code fixes alone cannot determine the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Narrow and stage
options.body: Split context packing from durable voice sessions, reuse existing Talk seams, and review each smaller product contract after the two blocking defects are repaired.

options.title: Keep the unified design
options.body: Retain the broad feature but require run-scoped authorization, reconnect-safe transcript identity, privacy/upgrade documentation, compiled native validation, and real behavior proof.

options.title: Defer the new surface
options.body: Keep current Talk behavior and decline the new persistent/configuration contract until a smaller sponsored design is agreed.

recommendation.title: Narrow and stage
recommendation.body: Split context packing from durable voice sessions, reuse existing Talk seams, and review each smaller product contract after the two blocking defects are repaired.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to cross-surface Talk product direction and Gateway architecture.
